_comment: Expectations for plumb_lines/examples/asm_kernels.rs (the library's default, stable asm! paths): python asm_check.py --package plumb_lines --example asm_kernels --toolchain stable. No TMR twins in that binary, so loop density is pinned with max_per_op at what the 2026-10 build gives (equal to TMR's twins where one exists in the bench: range flush 1.5 = flush_range_to_dram). Each asm! flush or NT store takes its address in a register (a lea), which is why the per-line wflush loop is looser than a range flush.
